column1: What is a decision problem (a language)?
column2: A yes/no question about strings. The language is the set of strings whose answer is yes.
A deterministic finite automaton: a fixed set of states, one move per input symbol, accept if it ends in an accepting state. Finite memory only.

column1: DFA rule for binary numbers mod 3?
column2: State \( r \) is the value so far mod 3. Reading bit \( b \): \( r \to (2r + b) \bmod 3 \). Accept in state 0.
Regular expressions, NFAs and DFAs describe exactly the same languages: the regular languages.
A backtracking regex engine tries every way to split the input, so a pattern like \( (a+)+b \) on \( a^n \) takes about \( 2^n \) steps.

column1: Why is Go regexp safe from ReDoS?
column2: It follows the RE2 design: automaton simulation, guaranteed time linear in the input. It drops backreferences to keep that promise.

column1: Why is \( a^n b^n \) not regular?
column2: Pumping lemma: a DFA with \( p \) states repeats a state while reading \( a^p \), so it also accepts a string with extra a's. A finite machine cannot count without bound.

column1: What does a pushdown automaton add to a DFA?
column2: One stack. It decides the context-free languages, such as balanced parentheses and \( a^n b^n \).
A finite rule table plus an endless tape and a head that reads, writes and moves. Church-Turing thesis: it computes anything an algorithm computes.
No program decides, for every program P and input x, whether P halts on x (Turing, 1936). Proof: a diagonal program D does the opposite of the prediction about itself.
Every nontrivial question about what a program does (its behavior, not its text) is undecidable.
P: solvable in polynomial time. NP: a yes answer has a short certificate that is checkable in polynomial time.
It is in NP, and every NP problem reduces to it in polynomial time. Cook-Levin: SAT is NP-complete.

column1: How does 3-SAT reduce to independent set?
column2: One triangle per clause, an edge between each literal and its opposite. Satisfiable exactly when an independent set of size (number of clauses) exists.

column1: What is a 2-approximation for vertex cover?
column2: Take a maximal matching and keep both ends of every matched edge. The cover is at most twice the optimum.
